evaluation.final_reason: No substantive settlement was reached by the end of Round 12. Agent D firmly refuses to have alcohol served in the flat for religious reasons (e.g. "It's because I'm Muslim... and I'm not comfortable with it being served in the flat for a party we're all hosting"). Agent A insists the alcohol was purchased personally and that the group should find a compromise rather than cancel (e.g. "I've already bought all of it with my own money..." and "we have to figure out how to compromise when we disagree"). Because the main incompatible demands (A wants alcohol available at the party; D refuses any alcohol being served in their shared home) remain, the disagreement is unresolved.

substantive_insights: Conflict hinges on a values clash (D's religious prohibition on alcohol) versus practical/social expectations (A's purchase and B's expectations at work).
A concrete financial fact (A already bought drinks and cannot return them) raises the cost of accommodating D, and D's offer to pay for the drinks is an attempt to remove that obstacle.
One roommate (B) retracts their preference under moral/communal pressure; another roommate (C) proposes avoiding alcohol for this event to prioritize long-term cohabitation stability.
No final arrangement was agreed: the conversation centers on whether individual religious convictions about the home should override a jointly-hosted event's expectations.
